summary: Round 5 plan check, 03:15-03:30Z on 26 Sep. The operations are sound. Commit f05389e (CLARIFICATION v2 and the provisional tick rule) landed at 01:20:05Z, before any score, and it is pushed. The poller (PID 20052) is alive with a 602 s cycle; its last poll was 03:13:26Z. #37 K2 and #38 twin are PENDING with the correct families. The laptop is on AC with sleep set to never, and no reboot is pending. The C2 error-class command works (kaggle 2.2.4). Memory files are current. Five issues remain. (1) PC5-01, today: the runtime-trigger contingency, 'move BOTH deadlines to 32400/37800 or D4', cannot be built. The builder refuses REPAIR_DEADLINE_S != 34200 on non-lab builds (build_probe_kernel.py l.2021-2022). D4 (DIVINS_TWOSTAGE) has no code. The only variant the builder accepts is DIVINS alone, which v4 forbids. No rule chooses between a deadline-moved K2' and K2. P(L(K2) > 8.0 h) is material: F = 7.87 h leaves 0.13 h to the insertion gate. (2) PC5-02, now: the C6 manual polls depend on the main session being awake at 07:45-08:01Z. A background one-shot script, stamped AFTER the CLI call, removes that dependency. Never import lb_poll.py for this, because its while-True loop runs at module level. (3) PC5-03, today: the 01:20 FINALS-TICK CHECKLIST says 'Never tick #34'. That contradicts C3, row 4 and f2, which keep #34 as the last resort. Row 4's no-K1 branch also gives F2 = exp52 where C3 and f2 give F2 = twin. (4) PC5-04, today: row 5's heuristic 'L(twin) >= L(K2) - 0.3 h means queue dominates' is mis-specified. K2 and the twin share their queue (#34/#35 ran concurrently), so their gap measures the insertion runtime cost. The correct paired bound is runtime(K2) <= L(K2)_hi - L(twin)_lo + 6.56 h. (5) PC5-05, now: the consolidated OK request (WATCHLIST W45) is still unrecorded; it should be posted and time-stamped before the twin's earliest score (~06:15Z). Info: the ledger's A6 text is stale ('K1 ... rebase K3 on K1'), and A5-F reads 'not supplied' although F = 7.87 h. No K3/K3b/forkblob/K4 proposals.

findings.what: The C6 manual 'clean-proof' polls (~07:57:30Z and ~08:00:45Z, if K2 is still PENDING at 07:45Z) depend on the main session being awake and free at 07:45-08:01Z. Research round 6 (~05:45Z) or a compaction can overlap that window. Two traps. (a) lb_poll.py runs its while-True loop at module level, so `import lb_poll` (to reuse poll()) would start a second infinite poller that also writes into poll.log. (b) lb_poll stamps the header BEFORE the CLI call. The ledger's upper bound adds 210 s per FAILED attempt but not the duration of the successful call. Near the 08:02:12Z mark a manual poll should therefore stamp AFTER the call returns. That is conservative for COMPLETE, which is the only case that matters; a PENDING result at 07:57-08:01 proves nothing either way. The ledger accepts any note text (failed attempts are counted only by '[empty stdout' / '[ERROR') and sorts polls by timestamp. Expected poller polls: ~07:54:2xZ and ~08:04:3xZ (602 s cycle from 03:13:26Z).

import datetime as d, os, pathlib, subprocess, sys, time
LOG = pathlib.Path('experiments/lb_poll/poll.log')
CMD = [sys.executable, '-m', 'kaggle', 'competitions', 'submissions', 'biohub-cell-tracking-during-development', '-v']
ENV = dict(os.environ, PYTHONIOENCODING='utf-8')
for hms in ('07:57:30', '08:00:45'):
    t = d.datetime.strptime('2026-09-26T' + hms + 'Z', '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ').replace(tzinfo=d.timezone.utc)
    while d.datetime.now(d.timezone.utc) < t: time.sleep(5)
    try:
        p = subprocess.run(CMD, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=100, env=ENV, encoding='utf-8')
    except Exception as e:
        print('manual poll failed', e); continue
    ts = d.datetime.now(d.timezone.utc).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')  # stamped AFTER the call
    if p.stdout.strip():
        with LOG.open('a', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            f.write(f'=== {ts} [manual one-shot, stamped after call]\n' + '\n'.join(p.stdout.strip().splitlines()[:60]) + '\n')

findings.what: Row 5's runtime diagnostic, 'raise the runtime trigger ... after comparing L(twin): L(twin) >= L(K2) - 0.3 h means queue delay dominates' (l.2002-2003), is mis-specified. Submissions on this account run CONCURRENTLY. #34 (08:09Z) and #35 (08:33Z) both finished by 16:17Z, whereas serial runs would have ended at >= ~20:45Z. So K2 and the twin, submitted 6 s apart, share essentially the same queue delay, and L(K2) - L(twin) measures the insertion RUNTIME cost, not queue. That cost is 0.26-1.44 h on the LB (L35 - L34 bounds), and the dummies show 1,512 s vs 1,038 s kernel end (repair 509 vs 219 s). A gap <= 0.3 h is roughly the no-queue normal case, so it cannot say 'queue dominates'. The informative quantity is L(twin) against the twin's own runtime. The twin is x138 + lowrefine (~0 cost) + inert safetail, whose runtime is <= L34_hi = 6.46 h plus ~0.1 h start jitter (818-1179 s across identical dummies). Paired bound under the equal-queue assumption: runtime(K2) <= L(K2)_hi - L(twin)_lo + 6.56 h. Worked example: L(K2) in (8.1, 8.3], L(twin) in (7.4, 7.6] gives runtime(K2) <= 8.3 - 7.4 + 6.56 = 7.46 h, so the insertion gate almost surely did not fire, although CLEAN (L <= 8.0 h) fails. Conversely, L(twin) ~6.5 with L(K2) > 8.0 means K2's own runtime is long, and the private tail probably lost the insertion.
